newsitem.title: GERMANY: Slow German chocolate sales add to cocoa mkt lull.
newsitem.headline: Slow German chocolate sales add to cocoa mkt lull.

text.p: German chocolate manufacturers are reporting unsatisfactory chocolate sales and this is contributing to hesitant cocoa bean purchases, physical traders said on Thursday.
"Easter chocolate sales were not as good as hoped this year because of the cold weather and because of the early date," one said.
The Easter holidays this year were in late March rather than April.
At that time, employees have usually received certain bonuses in their April pay and regain their purchasing power after spending sprees before Christmas.
Traders said only small bean parcels sold if they were discounted.
Industrial and trade buyers had made some purchases for fourth quarter 1997 and first quarter 1998 in the second week of April when the second futures position hit 962 stg.
By comparison, July on the London futures exchange last was at 1,038 stg, unchanged from Wednesday.
Supply of beans and butter was described as comfortable.

Cocoa butter sellers were offering a much reduced ratio of 2.41 over futures for the second quarter and 2.44 for the third quarter, with the implied mark price 7.08 marks/kg liquid ex-works in the third quarter.
A month ago, the ratio for 1997 dates was in a 2.54-2.58 range.
Second quarter 1997 cif Ivorian bean sellers were at 2.81-2.86 marks/kg and third quarter 1997 beans were at around 2.85 marks.
Sterling was at 2.7775 marks at the Frankfurt Exchange Fixing at midday.
